summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled 'Book 10 — part 143') following Leon, who meticulously avoids the childhood habits he once had, such as being the messy 'Hansel and Gretel' kid, and who plans to sell something new to a wealthy man in a vat aiming for life eternal among machines. The passage also describes the shifting character of the Lower East Side over the years and the changing stock of its corner shops, which Leon reads as a sign of coming change. It ends with a backstory of his parents, who emigrated from Romania to Anguilla and ended up in a vertical slum, and it breaks off mid-sentence.
one_line: Excerpt from a near-future novel following Leon, a meticulous man haunted by his childhood, as he plans a sale to a wealthy man in a vat.
key_facts: Leon stops at the grocer's every night to buy anything that ran out the previous day.
His parents came to visit from Anguilla and teased him about how organized he was.
Leon's sixth grade teacher awarded him the "Hansel and Gretelprize" for leaving a trail behind him everywhere he went.
Leon's organized habits are the product of an iron determination not to be the fat little boy he once was.
Leon plans to figure out how to sell something new to the man in the vat.
The man in the vat hopes to go down to life eternal in an ever-expanding kingdom of machines.
The Lower East Side has ebbed and flowed over the years between poor, rich, middle-class, super-rich, and poor.
Walking around his neighborhood, Leon sniffed change in the wind.
The shopkeepers seemed to have more discount, high-calorie wino-drink and less designer low-carb energy food.
Leon's parents emigrated from Romania to Anguilla, chasing the tax-haven set.
Leon's parents arrived in the middle of an econopocalyptic collapse and ended up living in a vertical slum that had once been a luxury hotel.
The Romanian parents were the sole Romanians among smuggled Mexicans who were de-facto slaves.
Leon didn't mind the neighborhood changes because he had lived rough himself.
